description: Three oscillators with a reading for each, every one driving two wave outputs that can be mixed or ring modulated against the oscillator's own carrier

params.text: Sets how far that oscillator's carrier swings, -10V to 10V
Shifts that oscillator's carrier round its cycle, -360 to 360 degrees
Adds a fixed voltage to that oscillator's carrier, -10V to 10V
Picks the wave shape of that output: SIN, TRI, SAW or SQR
Sets the extra shaping of that output, 0% to 100%; on a square wave it is the duty cycle
Shifts that output round its cycle, -360 to 360 degrees, on top of the oscillator's own phase
Sets how much of the modulated signal is mixed into the modified output, 0% for the raw wave alone and 100% for the modulated one alone
Switches that output's modulation between digital multiplication and ring modulation against the oscillator's carrier
Restarts the oscillator below from the start of its cycle whenever this oscillator passes its own start

inputs.text: Sets that oscillator's amplitude, added to the amplitude knob
Sets that oscillator's frequency, added to the frequency knob
Shifts that oscillator's carrier round its cycle, added to the phase knob
Adds a voltage to that oscillator's carrier, added to the offset knob
A rising edge here restarts that oscillator from the start of its cycle
Picks that output's wave shape over -5V to 5V, added to the wave knob
Sets that output's extra shaping, added to the aux knob
Shifts that output round its cycle, added to its phase knob
Sets how much of the modulated signal is mixed into the modified output, added to the mod knob

outputs.text: Sends a pulse each time that oscillator passes the start of its cycle
Carries that output's wave on its own, with no modulation applied
Carries that output's wave after the oscillator's carrier has been mixed or ring modulated into it

notes: each oscillator has a carrier of its own, set by the four knobs on its top row, and the two rows beneath it are the waves that carrier modulates
the raw output is the wave by itself and the modified output is the same wave with the carrier applied, so patching the raw jack gives an ordinary oscillator
the readings beside each oscillator show the four carrier values on the top line and the two output waves on the lines beneath
